question: Sultan Muhammad Bin Tughluq appointed ____________, a wine distiller, to a high administrative post in the Delhi Sultanate.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Aziz Khummar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• Aziz Khummar was a wine distiller appointed by Sultan Muhammad Bin Tughluq.

• Muhammad Bin Tughluq was known for his eccentric and unorthodox decisions, including appointing people from various unconventional backgrounds to high administrative posts.

• His reign (1325-1351) saw several controversial and radical policies which often led to mixed outcomes.

• Aziz Khummar's appointment is often cited as an example of Muhammad Bin Tughluq's unconventional approach to governance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Muhammad Bin Tughluq**

• Muhammad bin Tughluq was the Sultan of Delhi from 1325 to 1351.

• He was the eldest son of Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq, the founder of the Tughlaq dynasty.

• His reign is marked by ambitious projects and experiments, some of which were ahead of their time.

• Notable projects include the transfer of the capital from Delhi to Daulatabad, introduction of token currency, and plans for agricultural reforms.

• **Delhi Sultanate**

• The Delhi Sultanate refers to the various Muslim dynasties that ruled in India from 1206 to 1526.

• It was established after the defeat of Prithviraj Chauhan by Muhammad of Ghor.

• The Sultanate saw the rule of several dynasties including the Mamluk, Khilji, Tughlaq, Sayyid, and Lodi dynasties.

• It played a crucial role in the cultural and political development of the Indian subcontinent during the medieval period.

• **Administrative Reforms of Muhammad Bin Tughluq**

• He introduced several administrative changes aimed at centralization and efficiency.

• His decision to introduce token currency (copper and brass coins) was a failure due to counterfeiting.

• The shifting of the capital to Daulatabad aimed at better control over the Deccan region but was eventually reversed due to logistical challenges.

• His attempts at agrarian reforms included tax increases and land revenue assessments, which led to widespread discontent among peasants.
